title: AM I IN THE PLACE OF GOD?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But Joseph said to them, 'Don't be afraid. Am I in the place of God?'" — Gen 50:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Am I in the place of God?"

This is the sentence that makes forgiveness possible. Joseph refuses the judge's seat. Whatever happened to him, punishing his brothers is not his job — and he knows it.

Most of our unforgiveness comes from quietly occupying a chair that is not ours. We hold the record. We decide the sentence. We determine whether the person has suffered enough yet. And the weight of that role is crushing, because we were never designed to carry it.

Paul quotes God's own words on the matter: "It is mine to avenge; I will repay" (Rom 12:19). That is not a threat; it is a release. You can step down. Justice will be done, and it will be done by Someone who sees perfectly and judges rightly — which you and I cannot.

Notice Joseph's first two words as well: "Don't be afraid." The forgiven need to hear it, sometimes repeatedly.

And here is the deepest comfort. The judgement we deserved did fall — on Christ, at the cross. God did not overlook sin. He bore it Himself. That is why we can let go of the sentence we were holding over someone else.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you sitting in the judge's seat over someone?
2. What would it feel like to hand that role back to God?
3. Who needs to hear "don't be afraid" from you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I have been holding a seat that belongs to You. I hand back the right to judge and repay. Free me from the weight of it, and let me speak peace instead. Amen.
